commitResults.messageTitle: Cap phone and email length before validation
commitResults.messageBody:
A phone of about 5000 digits was accepted by add, but the next launch
crashed with a StackOverflowError while loading the data file, and no
.bak copy was made. The phone regex recursed once per digit, and data
loading runs on a thread with a smaller stack than the UI thread. Long
emails had the same problem through the local-part regex.

Phone numbers are now capped at 30 characters and emails at 254, the
practical limit for an email address. The length is checked before
any regex runs, so an over-long value from a command or from the data
file gets the normal constraint message, and loading falls back to
the .bak path instead of crashing.

The phone regex is also rewritten to use a lookahead plus a character
class, which accepts the same inputs but matches in a loop, so it
cannot overflow even without the length cap.
Avoid duplicate tags that differ only by case

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject a blank follow-up date on add
commitResults.messageBody:
Typing f/ with nothing after it on add showed the DD-MM-YYYY format
error, which suggests the date was written wrongly. On edit the same
input clears the follow-up, so users may expect it to mean "no
follow-up" on add too.

Check for a blank value first and tell the user to leave out f/
instead. Edit keeps its current behaviour, where a blank f/ clears the
date.

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept due days with any number of leading zeros
commitResults.messageBody:
The days argument was limited to 9 characters so Integer.parseInt
could not overflow. That also rejected values such as 0000000365,
which are in range, while 000000365 was accepted.

Strip leading zeros first and limit the remaining digits to the length
of MAX_DAYS. Overflow is still impossible, and the result no longer
depends on how many zeros were typed.

commitResults.messageTitle: End the due days error with a full stop
commitResults.messageBody:
The other parser errors end with a full stop, but the invalid days
message for due did not. Add it, and update the DG manual test that
quotes the message so testers see the exact text.

commitResults.messageTitle: Sort due ties by name with a collator
commitResults.messageBody:
Contacts due on the same date were ordered with CASE_INSENSITIVE_ORDER,
which compares UTF-16 values, so a name such as Émile Tan came after
Zack Lim. Names may start with accented letters, so this looked wrong.

Use a Collator for Locale.ROOT, which puts accented letters next to
their base letter and does not depend on the user's locale.

commitResults.messageTitle: Format due counts with the root locale
commitResults.messageBody:
String.format uses the default locale, so on a machine set to a locale
such as ar-EG the due count was printed in Arabic-Indic digits and the
due tests failed. The app's messages are English, so the count should
always use ASCII digits.

Pass Locale.ROOT to both due messages and add a test that runs the
command under ar-EG.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test DueCommand equality with another day's clock
commitResults.messageBody:
DueCommand.equals compares the clock as well as the number of days,
but no test used a different clock, so dropping the clock check went
unnoticed. hashCode and toString were never run either.

Add an equals case with a clock one day later, and cover hashCode and
toString.

commitResults.messageTitle: Pin the time zone used by parsed due commands
commitResults.messageBody:
The parser tests compared two commands built with the default clock,
so they would still pass if DueCommand switched to a UTC clock. For
users in Singapore that would make due a day behind each morning.

Build the expected commands with Clock.systemDefaultZone() explicitly,
and add a test that sets the default zone to Pacific/Kiritimati and
checks the parsed command uses it and not UTC. The test does not
depend on the zone the tests run in.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the missing fields when add is incomplete
commitResults.messageBody:
An add command without one of n/, p/, e/ or a/ showed only the
generic usage text, so the user had to work out which field was
left out. The use case says the app should explain which details
need correction.

Report the missing prefixes first, in the order of the command
format, followed by the usage on the next line. Text before the
first prefix still shows the usage alone, since it is unclear which
field it was meant for.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify tag rules and accept accented letters
commitResults.messageBody:
Tags used the ASCII-only \p{Alnum} pattern, so t/café was rejected
even though names accept accented letters, and every tag error showed
the terse "Tag names should be alphanumeric" with no full stop.

Tags are still a single word of letters and digits, but letters and
digits now mean any Unicode letter or digit, matching names. Input is
normalised to NFC first, so a decomposed accent is the same tag as the
composed one.

Tag equality now compares the lower-cased name (Locale.ROOT) in both
equals and hashCode, so they agree for non-ASCII case pairs such as
the Turkish dotted and dotless i. The list t/ filter uses the same
rule.

The constraint message now states the rule with an example, and the
user guide add section lists what a tag may contain.

commitResults.messageTitle: Pin the data file's JSON key names in tests
commitResults.messageBody:
The storage tests only save and load through the same adapter classes,
so renaming a key such as status, followUp or interactionNotes in
JsonAdaptedPerson kept every test green while users' saved data was
silently dropped on the next launch.

Add a hand-written fixture in the exact on-disk format, with one
contact that uses every field and one older contact without status,
followUp or interactionNotes. DataFileFormatTest loads it through
JsonAddressBookStorage and compares it with PersonBuilder contacts,
checks that the older contact falls back to PROSPECT with no follow-up
and no notes, and saves a known contact to check the written key names
with the Jackson tree model.

The key check only requires the expected keys to be present, so adding
a new field does not break it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject unusable GUI settings in preferences file
commitResults.messageBody:
A preferences.json with "guiSettings": null made the app crash on
launch. Jackson writes the null straight into UserPrefs, so no
DataLoadingException was raised, and initPrefs saved the null back.
Every later launch crashed until the user deleted the file by hand.

Window coordinates near the int limits also abort the app on macOS
inside the native window code, and null, zero, negative or non-finite
sizes give a broken window that is then saved again.

Let's check the GUI settings after reading the file and throw a
DataLoadingException when they are unusable. MainApp already handles
that exception by logging a warning, using the default preferences and
overwriting the bad file, so the app starts and recovers on its own.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make tag case matching consistent for Unicode
commitResults.messageBody:
Comparing lowercased names misses some case pairs that Unicode
letters bring in. The Greek capital sigma has two lowercase forms, so
"ΟΣ" and "οσ" were different tags. Lowercasing an NFC string can also
give a string that is not NFC, so U+03AA U+0301 did not equal its own
lowercase form and list t/ with that exact tag name missed it.

Build the comparison key by lowercasing, then uppercasing, with NFC
normalisation after each step. Variants that share an uppercase form
are now one tag, and equals, hashCode and the list filter all use the
same key. As a side effect "straße" and "STRASSE" are one tag, and the
dotless i matches I, as String.equalsIgnoreCase already did.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject emoji built from marks in tags
commitResults.messageBody:
A digit followed by U+FE0F and U+20E3 is the keycap emoji, but it
passed the tag check because any combining mark was allowed after the
first character. A trailing variation selector could also make an
invisible difference between two tags that look the same.

Allow only non-spacing and spacing combining marks, and leave out the
variation selectors, so vowel signs in Hindi, Tamil and Thai still
work. Add TagTest cases for zero-width characters, emoji, digits from
other scripts, Tamil, a 1000 character tag and a prefix-like tag.
Add integration tests for command sequences

commitResults.messageTitle: Check the fraction of a second in saved notes
commitResults.messageBody:
The save test only checked a note timestamp with no fraction, so
saving timestamps rounded down to whole seconds went unnoticed. Also
use Status.DEFAULT instead of a hard-coded status name.

commitResults.messageTitle: Cap window size read from the preferences file
commitResults.messageBody:
A huge window height with an ordinary y position still pushed the
native window frame past the int range and aborted the app on every
launch. Reject sizes above 1,000,000 like the coordinates. Also let
the throw helpers use assertThrows and name the boundary test.

commitResults.messageTitle: Cap tag length and tighten tag characters
commitResults.messageBody:
Case mapping a long tag was very slow, because lowercasing a run of
Greek sigma gets slower the longer the run is. The case-insensitive
key was also worked out again on every equals and hashCode call, so a
single 100k character tag could stall add, list t/ and startup for
minutes.

Tags are now capped at 50 characters, counted after composing
accents, and the length is checked before any other work. The key is
worked out once when the tag is made, and the list filter compares
these keys, so t/STRASSE and t/straße also give equal filters. Plain
ASCII tags skip normalization and the pattern, which keeps loading a
large data file as fast as before.

Tags also accepted characters that draw nothing, such as the Hangul
fillers, the combining grapheme joiner and the Mongolian variation
selectors, plus unlimited stacks of combining marks. These are now
rejected, with at most two marks on each letter. Digits must be
decimal digits, so number symbols such as one half, superscript two
and circled one are rejected.

An old data file with a tag over 50 characters fails to load, so it
is copied to the usual .bak file and the app starts empty, like any
other invalid data file.

commitResults.messageTitle: Look up the list tag filter in the tag set
commitResults.messageBody:
Tags now keep their case-insensitive key and use it for both equals
and hashCode, so a contact's tag set can answer the list t/ filter
with one lookup instead of checking every tag in turn. With 200 tags
per contact this makes the filter about ten times faster.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove an unused tag comparison helper
commitResults.messageBody:
Only the tests called it. equals and hashCode already use the same
cached key, and the tests now check equality directly.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test that sort order affects model equality
commitResults.messageBody:
ModelManager.equals compares the displayed list, so two models with the
same contacts but a different active sort order should not be equal.
Command tests rely on this when they compare against an expected model,
yet nothing failed if equals ignored the order.

Add a test that sorts one model in reverse name order, checks that it
is not equal to an unsorted copy, then resets the filter and checks
that the two are equal again.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix data transfer steps in the UG FAQ
commitResults.messageBody:
The FAQ told users to overwrite the data file the app creates on the
new computer. A fresh install does not create data/addressbook.json
until a command changes contact data, so there was nothing to
overwrite. Read-only commands such as list do not create it either.

Tell users to create the data folder themselves and copy their old
addressbook.json into it while the app is closed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Correct when the DG says the data file is recreated

Commands that do not change contact data no longer save, so list does

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject trailing content in JSON data files
commitResults.messageBody:
JsonUtil read data files with ObjectMapper#readValue, which stops after
the first JSON value. A data file with a second address book, a stray
brace or other text after the closing brace loaded only the first part
without any error. No backup was made, and the next save overwrote the
file, so the extra contacts were lost.

Read the value through a JsonParser and require that only whitespace
follows it. Anything else now fails with an IOException that gives the
line and column of the extra content, so readJsonFile throws
DataLoadingException and the usual backup and empty start path runs.
This covers both the address book and the preferences file.

Jackson 2.7 has no FAIL_ON_TRAILING_TOKENS, so the check is done by
hand instead of upgrading Jackson.

commitResults.messageTitle: Mention trailing text in data file guide
commitResults.messageBody:
Extra text after the final closing brace of the data file now makes the
file invalid. Say so in the sentence that explains the backup, so users
who paste contacts after the brace know why the app started empty.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add planned enhancements appendix to DG
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG has no Planned Enhancements appendix yet. Known flaws that we
will not fix before the feature freeze can still be reported as bugs
in the PE.

Add the appendix after the manual testing appendix. It states the team
size and lists 10 enhancements, the maximum for a team of 5. Each item
gives the current behaviour with the exact message, and the planned
change with sample input and output.

The items cover the data file being overwritten by a second window or
a hand edit, prefix parsing (capitalised prefixes, a/l and a/p in
names, tabs), index checks (missing space, very large numbers,
non-ASCII digits), and the clear, find and edit messages.
